citation.author: Bagnoli, Nicolas
citation.title: How Video Games Reflect a Discourse About Another Era: The Case of Red Dead Redemption II
citation.type: MA thesis (Master en Communication Multilingue, Universite de Liege; promoters Fanny Barnabe and Marie Herbillon)

discipline: Francophone game studies / media-and-communication discourse analysis (ludo-narrative method)
thesis: RDR2, though set at the turn of the twentieth century, conveys a discourse about the player's own contemporary era by embedding modern values (feminism, anti-racism, the animal/ecological cause) into a historically distant setting, chiefly via Bogost's procedural rhetoric (above all the honor system) working in concert with avatar, cut-scenes, interactivity, environment, components and PNJs to remediatize some stereotypes and deconstruct others.
sections: Part 1: The specific features of RDR2 (Rockstar/Houser production context; crunch; American video games per Seydoux; open-world action/adventure)

Part 1 cont.: features of the game object (ludo-narrative conflict; concept of video game = information/environment/components/virtual interface/characters; the avatar/avatar-marionnette; rules & gameplay; narrative aspect; movies & video games, GTA license, western parallelism, cut scenes)
Part 2: Video games ideology and discourse (discourse; presuppose & sous-entendu per Krieg-Planque)

Part 2 cont.: procedural rhetoric (Bogost, McDonald's Videogame); layering values; interactivity; ideology (Marx/Althusser, America's Army); morality (Moore/Sicart/Bogost); RSA & ISA (police, army, church, family); stereotypes
Part 3: The means put in place to deliver a discourse in RDR2 (seven worked scene-analyses)

Part 3 scenes: 2.1 suffragette + Course of True Love march; 2.2 eugenics supporter Norris Forsythe; 2.3 the Ku Klux Klan; 2.4.1 the French (Charles Chatenay); 2.4.2 the Italians (Angelo Bronte); 2.5 the animal cause / Albert Mason; 2.6 random PNJ conversation (Sampson Black trial); 2.7 Red Skins vs. US Army (Wapiti/Rains Fall/Favours)

concepts.gloss: Bogost's notion that games mount arguments through the authorship of rules of behavior and dynamic models, not through words or images; the load-bearing concept of the thesis, applied above all to the honor system.

RDR2's procedural value-meter: rises for greeting/helping and for killing KKK members, falls for killing innocents/dogs/horses/over-hunting; read as a polarized but choice-preserving system; absent in main missions.
concepts.locus: Part 1 sec. 1.1 (p.9); Part 2 sec. 3 (pp.41-43); Part 3 passim

concepts.gloss: Same act (killing law officers) is unpunished in missions but honor-penalized in free roam; procedural rhetoric thus sends a conflicting message that wrongdoing is tolerated when scenario-justified.
The game re-circulates ('remediatizes') national stereotypes (British/French/Italian) but actively dismantles ('deconstructs') the Indian 'savage' stereotype; the central interpretive axis of Part 3.
Fanny Georges's category for a predefined avatar (Arthur Morgan): customizable only in clothes/guns/hair, carrying a fixed progressive disposition independent of player choice.

Krieg-Planque's two implicit-persuasion techniques (context-independent presupposition vs. interpretation-dependent insinuation) used to parse in-game dialogue (e.g., Norris Forsythe's racism by sous-entendu).

concepts.term: Ideological State Apparatuses (ISA) / Repressive State Apparatuses (RSA)
concepts.gloss: Althusser's distinction (ideology-operating institutions: church, family, school; violence-operating: police, army, courts), mapped onto RDR2 institutions; the camp read as a Family ISA.
After Barnabe/Hurel: narration and gameplay are not impermeable but constantly articulated; the ludology/narratology opposition is treated as past and set aside.
Lits via Hurel: every narrative carries an implicit worldview; RDR2's values are a layering of developers' and contemporary players' doxa onto the historical setting.

concepts.term: Five elements of the video-game concept
concepts.gloss: Hurel/Jarvinen taxonomy: information, environment, components, virtual interface, characters; the analytic vocabulary for locating ideology in game elements.
The player-as-camera movie-making affordance and the black bars that frame every NPC conversation; reinforce the western-filmic register and the cut-scene's value-delivering function.
The doctrine that the US was destined to expand and spread democracy/capitalism; invoked to frame both the suffrage scene and the Indian/Army conflict.

readings.claim: RDR2 says something about the player's present despite its turn-of-century setting; the game's world is a discourse about contemporary society.
The honor system is the game's primary procedural argument, coding dialogue as good and violence as bad to produce a polarized value system.
By permitting the 'bad' actions (unlike Horizon or Breath of the Wild), RDR2 valorizes not pacifism but the possibility of choice, though that free will is itself biased by punishment.
Arthur Morgan, as avatar-marionnette, carries a scripted progressive/anti-racist disposition the player cannot override; cut-scenes are where un-resistable values are delivered.
National/ethnic stereotypes (British eccentricity, French romantic narcissism, Italian mafia/spaghetti) are remediatized as recognizable cognitive shortcuts.
The Indian 'savage' stereotype is deliberately deconstructed via Rains Fall and the Wapiti missions, set against the army's conservative worldview.
Killing KKK members grants honor (and the Klan self-immolates without player action), encoding Rockstar's anti-KKK stance procedurally.
Albert Mason is a paradoxical/hypocritical conservationist (animals die for his photos; he ignores the boar eaten by the gator), satirizing contemporary animal-rights inconsistency.
In games generally religion is criticized (its abuses) while the army is valorized, so RDR2's criticism of each is not subversive in the same way.
The Van der Linde gang is a metaphorical Family-ISA; Dutch embodies anti-modern decadence ('crime as decadence' per Bogost) against Arthur's late-game moral turn.
RDR2 is historically accurate on facts (alligator near-extinction, suffrage timeline, Wounded Knee) but idealizes/satirizes the discourse layered atop them.
Gameplay functions as a staging tool; the Banking mission and cinema mode show Rockstar building a film out of play.

game_elements.how_treated: Read as the spine of RDR2's procedural rhetoric: a polarized good/bad value-meter that permits but penalizes violence, is absent in main missions, and rewards killing KKK members.
game_elements.locus: Part 1 p.9; Part 2 pp.41-44; Part 3 passim

game_elements.element: Interaction verbs (greet / antagonize / rob / aim weapon)
game_elements.how_treated: Free-roam dialogue system whose NPC reactions are contingent on the chosen verb; greeting raises honor, robbing/firing lowers it; scripted PNJs ignore the choice.
Paradigm case of open-world choice-with-consequence: four options (tonic, suck venom, leave to die, mercy-kill) each with honor and world effects.

game_elements.element: The Course of True Love (Chapter 2 mission)
game_elements.how_treated: Arthur drives a wagon of suffragists and must protect the march; no option to refuse, illustrating procedural compulsion in feminism discourse.
Scripted two-stage conversation delivering an early-feminist (somewhat caricatured) discourse; identical whether greeted or antagonized; harming her costs honor.
White-supremacist whose racism works by sous-entendu; gives a racist pamphlet (component); modeled to resemble Hitler; can be beaten/killed with no honor loss or police response.

game_elements.element: Ku Klux Klan encounters (x2, free-roam, Lemoyne)
game_elements.how_treated: Cross-burning ceremony that self-immolates without player action; killing members grants honor; lootable 'Meeting notes' letter ridicules the group; procedural mockery of organized religion.

game_elements.element: Charles Chatenay (French painter; 'The Artist's Way' quest line)
game_elements.how_treated: Bar meeting (only 'greet' available) and nude art-gallery exhibition scene; remediatizes the French stereotype (romantic, narcissistic, 'asshole').

game_elements.element: Angelo Bronte (Italian mafioso; Chapter 4 antagonist; mission #44 'A Man of Honor')
game_elements.how_treated: Italian-music cue, mafia dress/manner, bribes the mayor; kidnaps the gang's youngest boy (Jack) and betrays the gang; remediatizes the Italian-mafia/spaghetti stereotype.
Over-hunting incurs honor loss; killing horses and dogs penalized (dogs trigger sheriff/town hostility and lasting grudges); read as Rockstar's pro-animal procedural argument.
Wolves (Arcadia II) and alligator missions; read as paradoxical/hypocritical conservationist whose dialogue anchors the contemporary eco-discourse and historical extinction facts.

game_elements.element: Random PNJ conversation (Sampson Black trial, Rhodes)
game_elements.how_treated: Overheard debate between two strangers over a rigged trial of a black man; staged as conservative (racist) vs. progressive worldviews; environment-as-discourse.

game_elements.element: Red Skins vs. US Army strand (Wapiti Indians; Chapter 6)
game_elements.how_treated: Indians represented as peaceful (stereotype deconstructed); music underscores their pacifism; the army (Favours) depicted as treaty-breaking and venal.
Peace-seeking leader without war-paint or aggression; the figure through whom the 'savage' stereotype is dismantled.
Favours withholds vaccines/medicine and confiscates horses on behalf of oil-tycoon Cornwall to clear the (oil-rich) reservation; mispronounces Rains Fall's name; the venal-authority antagonist.
Player recovers Indian medicine stolen by Favours; opening calm music/animal noises emphasize Indian peacefulness.
Arthur escorts Rains Fall to the failed meeting with Favours; dialogue deconstructs the savage stereotype.

game_elements.element: Banking, the Old American Art (Chapter 4, mission #57)
game_elements.how_treated: The Saint-Denis bank robbery gone wrong (Pinkertons, rooftop escape, long pursuit); exemplar of gameplay-as-staging and cinema mode.
The camp read as a Family ISA; site of loyalty and the Dutch-vs-Arthur ideological opposition (anti-modern decadence vs. emergent conscience).
Anti-modernization 'return to nature' ideologue who becomes increasingly violent/decadent ('crime as decadence'); his greed precipitates the gang's fall.
Early unquestioning outlaw conditioned by Dutch; late-game (near death) acts on his own convictions, e.g., refusing to collect for Strauss and expelling him.
German loan-shark whose debts Arthur is sent to collect by force; Arthur's Chapter-6 refusal/expulsion marks his moral turn; stereotyped via name and accent.
Debauched former clergyman; instance of Rockstar mocking religion (Church ISA).
Utopian cult recruiting young men, encounterable only in main missions; player may strangle or talk down its leader; further religion satire.
Chapter-3 camp confrontation ('we didn't kill all them savages...') establishing the authorities' anti-Indian view and the encroachment of civilized land.

game_elements.element: He Is British, Of Course (side mission)
game_elements.how_treated: Retrieving a painted donkey 'zebra' for an eccentric Englishman; mission name itself read as an information-channel stereotype.
Player-as-camera affordance during long rides plus black bars on every NPC conversation; reinforce the western-filmic register and cut-scene value delivery.

game_elements.element: Western action vocabulary (horse shootings, cowboy duels, train robberies, bridge demolition)
game_elements.how_treated: Inherited Hollywood-western codes remediated in both gameplay and cut-scenes (Leone, Tarantino invoked).
Jarvinen's 'components' as value-bearing objects in the inventory; the eugenics pamphlet and KKK 'Meeting notes' are the worked cases.

game_elements.element: Setting / regions (Saint-Denis, Lemoyne, Rhodes; 6 chapters + epilogue)
game_elements.how_treated: Saint-Denis as the industrialized discourse-hub (suffragette, Norris, Chatenay, Bronte); Lemoyne swamps for gators; the chapter structure frames the analysis.

themes: race, eugenics, and white supremacy (KKK, Norris Forsythe, the Sampson Black trial)
the animal/ecological cause and conservationist hypocrisy
settler-colonial violence and Manifest Destiny (Wounded Knee)
satire, political correctness, and Rockstar's house style
the cinema-video game relationship and remediation of the western

interlocutors.name: Aki Jarvinen

interlocutors.name: Alexis Blanchet
interlocutors.why: Cinema-to-game borrowing of style/stereotypes; stereotype as narrative-economy device.

interlocutors.name: Katie Salen & Eric Zimmerman

interlocutors.name: Markku Eskelinen

interlocutors.name: Bob Rehak
interlocutors.work: 'Playing at Being: Psychoanalysis and the Avatar' (2003)
interlocutors.why: Avatar as the 'present one' and the cinematic-suture-plus formula 'Yes, that's what I do'; games vs. cinema on ideological positioning.

interlocutors.name: Miguel Sicart
interlocutors.why: Moral imperative inscribed in the character rather than transferred to the player; supports the non-normative reading of procedural morality.

interlocutors.name: J. Cameron Moore
interlocutors.work: Making Moral Choices in Video Games (2011)
interlocutors.why: Moral-choice RPGs (Fable, Mass Effect) as cultivating moral perception; framing for RDR2's choice system.

interlocutors.name: Alice Krieg-Planque
interlocutors.why: Presuppose and sous-entendu as implicit-persuasion techniques for dialogue analysis.

interlocutors.name: Ruth Amossy
interlocutors.why: Definition of stereotype (prejudice / cognitive generalization) underpinning the remediatization axis.

interlocutors.name: Mathieu Triclot
interlocutors.why: Game as 'instrumented experience'; brackets whether play is experienced as narrative.

interlocutors.name: Yves Chevaldonne
interlocutors.why: Game at the intertextual knot of cinema/comics/literature; cut-scene definition.

interlocutors.name: Marc Lits
interlocutors.why: Narrative as conveying a worldview (vision du monde).

interlocutors.name: Fanny Georges
interlocutors.why: Avatar typology incl. avatar-marionnette and empathic identification.

interlocutors.name: Dan Houser (interviews)
interlocutors.why: Authorial intent: western binge-watching, satire's limits, modern-values approach to history.

debate_axis_positions: Ludology vs. narratology: treats the opposition as past; sides with porosity (Barnabe/Hurel), declines to adjudicate whether players experience the game narratively.

Mechanics vs. fiction as locus of meaning: refuses the either/or; meaning emerges only from the co-operation of mechanics (honor, verbs, permissions), fiction (dialogue, cut-scenes, characters), and environment.
Value transfer to the player: foregrounds Bogost/Sicart caution; the honor system models morality arithmetically/linearly and inscribes values in Arthur rather than coercing the player.

Authenticity / historical representation: reads RDR2's period accuracy as the vehicle for deliberately anachronistic, present-day values; historically accurate on facts but idealizing/satirizing the layered discourse.
Satire vs. sincerity (Rockstar house style): RDR2 is more serious than prior Rockstar games yet retains satire (suffragette exaggeration, KKK/Chatenay ridicule, Albert Mason hypocrisy).
tensions: Procedural rhetoric vs. player freedom: the honor system is framed as valorizing 'the possibility of choice,' yet Bagnoli concedes that free will is itself biased because the system punishes 'bad' actions.

Layering of values is internally conflicting: killing law officers is 'profoundly wrong' yet 'tolerated' when scenario-justified, so the game's moral message is not consistent across missions vs. free roam.

Remediatization vs. deconstruction sit uneasily side by side: the same game that dismantles the Indian stereotype reinforces British/French/Italian ones, with no account of why some groups get critique and others caricature.
Bracketing of reception: the thesis insists the game conveys a discourse while admitting players may ignore narration entirely (speed-runners), leaving open whether the discourse actually lands.

Author's progressive avatar vs. satirical exaggeration: Arthur is read as sincerely progressive while the suffragette's idealism is read as purposely caricatured, a line the analysis does not fully reconcile.
Methodological selection bias: only 'meaningful' scenes with 'a lot to say' are analyzed, acknowledged as a curation that may overstate the coherence of the game's discourse.
Minor inaccuracies/OCR-level slips in the source (e.g., the diegesis variously dated XIXth/XXth century; 'Red Skins' as the author's term) flagged but not resolved.
